You are a large-language-model assistant asked to analyse a financial disclosure concerning Entergy Corporation’s wholesale-commodities (nuclear-power) business and to compute a specific figure.

Scenario context (excerpted from the company’s filing – no tabular data shown):
• Entergy Wholesale Commodities (EWC) owns and operates six nuclear power plants in the United States.  Revenues are primarily derived from selling electricity and generation capacity.  EWC also provides operations, management and decommissioning services to other utilities.
• For each plant, the filing discusses (among other things) the market in which it participates, the year the asset was placed in service, the year Entergy acquired the asset, and the expiry date of the current operating licence granted by the U.S. Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC).
• The operating licences for several plants (e.g. Pilgrim, Indian Point 2, Indian Point 3) were due to expire between 2012 and 2015.  Federal law allows operation beyond the stated expiry while a renewal application is pending.  Various parties have opposed renewals, triggering administrative and legal proceedings described in the document.
• In March 2011 the NRC renewed Vermont Yankee’s operating licence for an additional 20 years, extending its expiry to 2032.  Entergy submitted renewal applications for Indian Point 2 and 3 in April 2007; litigation of multiple contentions is ongoing.

Tools you may call (each returns JSON-serialisable values):
• search_plants_by_name(partial_name): list matching nuclear-plant names.  Useful when the exact spelling is uncertain.
• get_acquisitions_for_plant(plant_name): list of all historical acquisitions for the given plant, including acquirer and acquisition date.
• get_latest_acquisition_by_acquirer(plant_name, acquirer="Entergy Corporation"): ISO date string of Entergy’s most recent purchase of the plant.
• get_all_licenses_for_plant(plant_name): list of all licence records (type, start date, expiry date, status).
• get_current_license_expiry(plant_name): ISO date string representing the expiry date of the current NRC operating licence for the plant.
• extract_year(date_string): convert an ISO date (YYYY-MM-DD) to integer year.
• years_between(start_year, end_year): arithmetic helper that returns the difference in calendar years.
• get_market_description(market_code): description of a wholesale electricity market (informational).
• get_reactor_capacity(plant_name): gross electrical capacity of the reactor in megawatts (informational).

Question (answer with a single integer number of years):
What is the length of the lease for Pilgrim, in years?

Think step-by-step, invoke tools as needed, and produce the final answer as a plain integer so that it can be automatically verified.
